author: DIPAK K DASH
description: In a daring move, the Indian Navy successfully thwarted a pirate assault on the Golden Arsenal in the perilous Gulf of Aden. The ship’s crew effectively sought refuge within an impregnable citadel that the invaders could not penetrate. Currently, four vessels remain under the control of Somali pirates, with Indian nationals on three of them.
title: Captain moves crew to citadel, thwarts pirate assault on India-bound vessel

author: SHIVA RAJORA
description: The rollout of EPFO's new IT system has resulted in a substantial backlog of claim issues. Field officials are grappling with an increasing number of pending auto claims, which have lingered for over twenty days and are causing significant discomfort to members. EPFO admits that this surge in pendency is a short-term effect of the system transition, although it was executed with minimal disruption to services.
title: EPFO, officers' body contest claims about new IT system

author: SURENDRA SINGH
description: India successfully tested its Agni-4 medium-range ballistic missile last Thursday.  This missile bridges a critical gap in India's strategic deterrence capabilities.  The Agni-4 missile can carry nuclear and conventional payloads with a 4,000 km range.  It features an advanced heat shield and a precise guidance system for accuracy.  This successful test reaffirms India's commitment to national defense technologies.
title: Agni-4 fills key gaps in India's missile arsenal, strengthens China deterrence

author: TOI SPORTS DESK
description: Ravindra Jadeja entertained teammates by mimicking Kuldeep Yadav’s bowling action, leaving Gautam Gambhir laughing during India’s Colombo warm-up match. Devdutt Padikkal impressed with an unbeaten 142, boosting his chances for the opening Test. Jadeja scored 63 and Manav Suthar added 41 as India reached 357/6. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel disappointed, managing just two and one respectively.

author: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA
description: The United States has firmly rejected China's maneuvers at Scarborough Reef, asserting that Beijing's environmental assertions are hindering Filipino fishermen from accessing their traditional fishing grounds. As a staunch ally in the Indo-Pacific, Washington stands in solidarity with the Philippines, highlighting China's contentious approach of using legal claims to assert maritime rights. This reaffirmation underscores US commitment to its allied nation's interests amidst complex maritime disputes.
title: US rejects China’s attempt to enforce new restrictions at Scarborough Reef

author: PRABIN KALITA
description: India has finalized its official mapping of the contested frontier areas of Arunachal Pradesh, encompassing crucial sites such as Asaphila and Maja. In response, the People's Liberation Army of China has erected various structures and roadways in these disputed territories. Historical conflicts have marked this sensitive border, and this mapping initiative effectively bolsters India's stance regarding the ongoing territorial dispute.
title: Latest Arunachal map shows 3 places illegally held by China

author: TNN
description: Union minister Kiren Rijiju called on LoP Rahul Gandhi to back the women's reservation bill during their exchange. In response, Rahul Gandhi noted that the 2023 bill had already received unanimous approval. He raised concerns about the holdup in implementing the legislation and its connection to the delimitation process. Gandhi insisted on prompt action to enforce the 2023 law, underscoring the heated political discourse on women's empowerment.
title: Rijiju, Rahul trade barbs over women's quota bill rollout

author: MANASH PRATIM GOHAIN
description: India's education funding aligns with GDP standards but falls short of public spending goals. Completion rates for secondary schools lag behind national and UNESCO guidelines. This funding pattern emerges as countries shift focus from education financial targets. India's extensive education initiatives benefit millions of students, yet the sector continues to grapple with persistent challenges despite increased program deployment.
title: Government spending on education below Unesco's 15% standard

author: KUMAR RAKESH
description: Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal now supports the women's reservation law rollout.  This move signals the government's potential revival of the Constitution amendment bill.  The government is also seeking support from DMK and NCP(SP) for the measure.  The bill aims to increase Lok Sabha's strength by fifty percent.  Its timing remains uncertain as lawmakers consider summoning Parliament.

author: TNN
description: The government has pledged that the upcoming UPI merchant discount rate will be minimal. This fee will be applicable only to certain merchants and transactions that surpass a designated threshold. Importantly, person-to-person UPI payments will remain free for all users. This initiative is designed to enhance the sustainability of India’s digital payment ecosystem and facilitate service expansion into rural and semi-urban regions.
title: Proposed MDR for UPI transactions will be nominal, says government

author: TNN
description: The law ministry notified thirty new judges for four high courts on Saturday. Madras High Court received fifteen appointments, while Calcutta got eight and Karnataka six. Judicial officers and advocates were elevated to the benches, with most appointed as additional judges. Over sixty lakh cases are pending across India's twenty-five high courts. The law minister cited collegium delays for the significant number of vacancies.

author: SAURABH SINHA
description: During a turbulent flight from Phuket to Delhi, the captain of an Air India aircraft reportedly tested positive for psychoactive substances. The turbulence caused a significant scare, resulting in hospitalization for thirteen passengers and four crew members. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation is conducting a detailed investigation, and the flight crew has been suspended from flying duties as per standard procedures.

author: TNN

This innovative facility is expected to streamline small rocket launches and improve operational efficiency. The chosen operator will oversee all functional aspects, while Isro commits to providing technical training and guidelines during a specified duration. The initiative aims to elevate India's capabilities in small satellite launches.

author: SURENDRA SINGH
description: The Union government has formally named twenty-seven locations in Arunachal Pradesh. These places include memorials honoring Indian Army war heroes from past conflicts. Havildar Shere Thapa and Rifleman Jaswant Singh Rawat are among those recognized for bravery. Several strategically important mountain passes and a logistics hub were also officially identified. This action pays homage to soldiers who sacrificed their lives defending India's borders.

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: In a groundbreaking discovery, scientists have identified a deep-sea crustacean, the amphipod Hirondellea gigas, which uses aluminum to survive in the Mariana Trench, one of Earth's most extreme environments. Its unique aluminum-coated exoskeleton helps resist calcium dissolution under immense pressure, allowing it to thrive where life was previously deemed impossible. This remarkable adaptation showcases innovative survival mechanisms in the deep ocean.
title: Scientists uncover the aluminium shield helping a tiny crustacean survive

author: NASEER GANAI
description: In the period from January to July, Ladakh has welcomed a remarkable 330,332 tourists. Air travel continues to be the favored mode of access to this stunning union territory. Among road travelers, the route through Kashmir is increasingly popular over the Manali path. Enhanced infrastructure and well-planned events have fueled this tourism surge, with burgeoning homestays offering fresh job opportunities for the local community.

The brutal incident, which occurred on August 4, resulted in one man suffering life-threatening injuries. This alarming event follows a fatal encounter in April, highlighting ongoing violence linked to cow protection. Investigations into wrongful restraint and assault are currently underway.

author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
description: In a catastrophic turn of events, a diminutive moth has decimated vast stretches of Siberian forest, transforming them into a fire hazard of monumental proportions. The Siberian silk moth's caterpillar stage ravages tree needles, resulting in widespread die-offs over several years. Major outbreaks have persisted over the decades, decimating millions of hectares, and now this ecological calamity aligns with an urgent wildfire emergency that has meteorological implications.

author: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK
description: Madhuri Dixit and her husband, Dr Shriram Madhav Nene, have sold another apartment in Mumbai's upscale Juhu locality for Rs 4.40 crore, nearly 14 years after purchasing it for Rs 1.94 crore. The deal reflects a capital appreciation of around 127 percent, according to property registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix.
title: Madhuri sells Juhu apt for Rs 4.40cr after 14 years; earns 127% return

author: ARINDAM GHOSH
description: Tragically, Aaban Ahmed, the son of Atiq Ahmed, lost his life in a devastating road accident on Thursday. While his vehicle was found to contain personal belongings, including books by Fyodor Dostoevsky and Marjan Kamali, police clarified that these items were unrelated to the circumstances of the crash. The severe injuries Aaban suffered ultimately led to his untimely passing, while his associate Sonu remains in critical condition following the collision.
title: Dostoevsky, Tehran coup novels found in Atiq Ahmed's son's car

author: TNN
description: Concerns were voiced by the Delhi High Court regarding Jantar Mantar as a protest site, questioning why the city should endure interruptions from protests. A Dalit Christian group has sought permission to hold a peaceful demonstration on August 10, while the police have been tasked to provide clarity on the request by Saturday. Additionally, the Supreme Court is considering other potential protest locations.
title: 'Why should entire city suffer?' Delhi HC on plea for protest at Jantar Mantar
